findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext inside the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and in Terraform state, exposing long-lived AWS credentials to anyone with instance or state access.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's administrative interface to the entire internet.
Inbound TCP port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the web server to unrestricted access from any source on the internet; combined with the public subnet placement this maximizes attack surface.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a kms_key_id, so data at rest on the volume is unencrypted, risking exposure if the underlying storage or snapshots are accessed improperly.

findings.issue_category: unencrypted snapshot / inherited lack of encryption
findings.description: The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption settings, meaning the backup data is stored unencrypted and could be shared or exposed without protection.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially allowing unauthorized read/write access to sensitive network traffic logs.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads to the internet.
